title: How Prehistoric People Survived After One of the Worst Volcanic Eruptions in History - Nautilus
gist: The Kikai-Akahoya eruption around 5,250 BCE, a VEI 7 event off Kyushu, devastated the Japanese archipelago with earthquakes, tsunamis and meters of ash, per Lund University archaeologist Peter Jordan. The excerpt is paywalled before the survival findings.

insights.claim: The Kikai-Akahoya eruption around 5,250 BCE rated a 7 on the Volcanic Explosivity Index, which tops out at 8, and ravaged the Japanese archipelago.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Calibrates the scale of low-frequency catastrophic volcanic risk.
